items.author: x0d7x
items.body:
Currently, keybindings in OpenCode, such as `Ctrl+K` for the command dialog, are hardcoded. This can lead to conflicts with keybindings in other tools commonly used in the terminal, like tmux.

For example, many tmux users have `Ctrl+K` bound for pane navigation. This conflict prevents the OpenCode command dialog from being accessible when running OpenCode inside tmux.

It would be beneficial to allow users to configure keybindings through the `.opencode.json` configuration file to resolve such conflicts and allow for greater personalization.

Suggested approach: Add a section in the `.opencod
items.title: Feature Request: Make keybindings configurable

items.author: DanielFerreiraJorge
items.body:
Like opencode, claude code has a non-interactive mode with the "-p" flag. For people that has a Claude MAX subscription, the usage of the opus and sonnet through claude code is virtually limitless (not really, but it is very hard to reach the limit when on the 20x). The MAX subscription does not consume any API credits when using claude code. It would be a nice feature to use "claude -p" as a provider instead of having to configure a anthropic api key, this way people, like me that uses claude code and opus, and want to switch to opencode, can do it without spending extra API credits. 

Thanks
items.title: Support Claude Code non-interactive mode as a provider
